name: MathlibAnnex.DeterminantFrame.nearMaxFrames
title: The set of near-maximal dual frames

content.display_title: The set of near-maximal dual frames
content.one_sentence_role: Records a determinant deficit while keeping all dual rows contractive.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space, and fix an ordered basis $b=(b_j)_{j=1}^n$. Write $C_b:E\to\mathbb R^n$ for the coordinate isomorphism, defined by $x=\sum_{j=1}^n(C_bx)_j b_j$, and give its coordinate space the sup norm $\|c\|_\infty=\max_j|c_j|$ (zero in dimension zero). A frame is an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals, with no independence assumed. Its matrix and evaluation map are
$$M_F=(\ell_i(b_j))_{i,j},\qquad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_FC_bx.$$
The admissible frames form the product of closed dual unit balls
$$\mathcal U=\{F:\|\ell_i\|_{E^*}\le1\text{ for every }i\}.$$
The norm on $E$ need not be a coordinate sup norm. Write $D_b=\max_{F\in\mathcal U}|\det M_F|$. For any $\eta\in\mathbb R$, define a set of frames $\mathcal N_{b,\eta}$.
content.definition_explanation:
The complete defining set is
$$\mathcal N_{b,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U:D_b-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
content.assumptions: The space, basis and any real number $\eta$ are inputs. Neither $\eta\ge0$ nor $\eta<D_b$ is required to define this set.
content.conclusion: A frame belongs precisely when it is admissible and its absolute determinant is at least $D_b-\eta$. This definition neither chooses a frame nor asserts invertibility.
content.lean_realization_notes: For every real $\eta$, [compactness of the near-maximal set](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L396-L402) follows by intersecting compact $\mathcal U$ with the closed inequality set. If $\eta\ge0$, [nonemptiness with nonnegative deficit](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L404-L410) uses an absolute maximizing frame $F_*$, since $D_b-\eta\le D_b$. If $\eta<D_b$, membership gives $|\det M_F|\ge D_b-\eta>0$ and hence invertibility. These are separate consequences with different hypotheses.
